data.3-qhull-licence-verdict#3. Qhull licence: COPYING.txt (Qhull 2020.2, SPDX Qhull) allows copying, modifying and redistributing under five conditions: (1) keep all copyright notices, (2) ship the text with every copy and with every product that includes Qhull, (3) a modification notice naming who, when and why, (4) say where the original can be obtained, (5) no warranty. There is no copyleft: a Go translation is a permitted modified version, and BSD-licensed code may sit beside it. Verdict: porting is allowed. The obligation in (2) travels to every binary that links the port, so the port lives in its own repository and module (go-geometry/qhull, licence file COPYING.txt verbatim, NOTICE with the modification record “translated to Go by the go-geometry authors, , to reproduce SciPy 1.18.1 output in pure Go”), and only the packages that need Qhull import it. KDTree, distance, transform and predicates never import it.
data.4-exactness-decision-per-component#4. Ex: Component Decision Equality target Delaunay, ConvexHull, Voronoi, HalfspaceIntersection, SphericalVoronoi Exact port of libqhull_r 2020.2 (the subset in section 2.7) and of _qhull.pyx Same simplices, same row order, same neighbors, coplanar, good; equations, area, volume bitwise against the Linux x86-64 oracle (section 6). An independent exact-predicate implementation could only promise combinatorial equivalence; for cospherical input it would choose different simplices and every consumer test written against SciPy would break. QJ joggle Port qh_rand (Park–Miller, qh_RANDOMtype 5) and the seed logic of global_r.c:1734-1760 Bitwise: the default seed is 1, not the clock. QR0/QR-1 (clock seed) are accepted but not reproducible, as in SciPy. Delaunay transform Port of _get_barycentric_transforms (getrf, gecon, getrs; rcond < 1000·eps → NaN) using go-ndarray linalg Bitwise if go-ndarray’s getrf follows the oracle’s LAPACK for n ≤ 64; otherwise tolerance 4 ulp per entry, stated in the release. Exact predicates Independent, from Shewchuk 1997 and the public-domain predicates.c Exact signs (never a tolerance); used to validate everything else and by the MATLAB delta. KDTree / cKDTree Exact port of ckdtree/src and _ckdtree.pyx (BSD-3-Clause), including SciPy’s own heap (query.cxx:32-98) Distances bitwise. Indices identical, including ties, if the tree layout matches; the layout depends on std::partition and std::nth_element (build.cxx:103-121), which differ between libc++ and libstdc++. Decision: port libc++’s two algorithms (Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception, compatible), giving layout equality with libc++-built wheels (task K0 verifies which wheels those are). libstdc++ (GPL-3.0 with runtime exception) is not ported: against GCC-built wheels the result is equal up to the order of exactly tied neighbours, and weighted count_neighbors sums agree to tolerance (their summation order follows the layout). distance (pdist, cdist) Exact port of the C++ and C kernels Bitwise. The kernels reduce each pair left to right over the features and interleave 4 pairs (2 when weighted) for ILP (distance_metrics.h:49-170): SIMD goes across pairs, never across features, without FMA, so parity holds. distance single-pair functions, directed_hausdorff Port of the NumPy expressions over go-ndarray; directed_hausdorff shuffles with go-ndarray random (MT19937 RandomState, PCG64 Generator, both present) Bitwise where go-ndarray is bitwise with NumPy; norm follows go-ndarray. Rotation, Slerp, RigidTransform, geometric_slerp, procrustes Exact port of both backends Bitwise for elementwise operations (no FMA: every product that Go could fuse is wrapped in an explicit float64(...) conversion, the rule of the Go spec). align_vectors, procrustes and mean go through go-ndarray SVD/Eigh: parity is whatever that library guarantees, stated per release. RotationSpline Exact port; needs scipy.linalg.solve_banded Blocked on the go-scikit linear-algebra item providing solve_banded; scheduled last in its wave. MATLAB delta Independent implementation on the exact predicates (MATLAB is closed source) Combinatorial equivalence and invariants against MATLAB when available and Octave otherwise; delaunayn/convhulln/voronoin go through the Qhull port with MATLAB’s default options (to be read from MathWorks in task M5). Floating-point rule for the whole organization. The Go compiler may fuse x*y + z into an FMA on arm64, ppc64le, s390x and riscv64. Every arithmetic expression in a ported kernel and in the predicates wraps products in float64(...) so that the result does not depend on the architecture; a test per package runs the kernels on GOARCH=arm64 and amd64 and compares bits. Whether SciPy’s own arm64 builds contract FMA (clang’s default -ffp-contract=on) is not verified: task Q0 measures it. Until then the bitwise oracle is the Linux x86-64 wheel (baseline x86-64 has no FMA), and other platforms are compared combinatorially and to tolerance.
Repository Licence Content Imports go-geometry/predicates BSD-3-Clause (source is public domain) Expansion arithmetic; Orient2D/3D, InCircle, InSphere (adaptive, exact, fast); exact n-D orientation and in-sphere by expansion determinants — go-geometry/qhull Qhull (separate module) Port of libqhull_r 2020.2: option parser, Quickhull, merging, Delaunay/Voronoi/halfspace modes, joggle, incremental — go-geometry/kdtree BSD-3-Clause Port of cKDTree; replaces the working name nearest go-ndarray go-geometry/distance BSD-3-Clause Metrics, pdist/cdist/squareform, validity helpers, directed_hausdorff go-ndarray, go-simd go-geometry/transform BSD-3-Clause Rotation, Slerp, RotationSpline, RigidTransform go-ndarray go-geometry/spatial BSD-3-Clause, links qhull The scipy.spatial facade: Delaunay, ConvexHull, Voronoi, HalfspaceIntersection, SphericalVoronoi, Tsearch, Procrustes, GeometricSlerp; re-exports kdtree and distance qhull, kdtree, distance, predicates (tests), go-ndarray go-geometry/triangulation BSD-3-Clause The MATLAB delta: Triangulation, DelaunayTriangulation (incl. 2-D constrained, shared with item 13), AlphaShape, searchers, pdist2, inpolygon, polyarea; replaces the working name hull predicates, kdtree, distance, qhull (for convhulln/voronoin) Each repository: CLI-free library, 100 % statement coverage, fuzz corpus committed, govulncheck in CI, README + docs page + landing entry on each user-visible release.
data.6-validation-plan#6. Validation plan: Oracle. SciPy 1.18.1 wheels pinned by hash, driven from a Go program that generates inputs, runs the oracle and writes JSON fixtures (the oracle never runs from shell). Bitwise oracle: manylinux_2_28_x86_64; second oracle: macosx_arm64. Octave (and MATLAB when available) for the delta. SciPy’s own tests ported: test_qhull.py, test_kdtree.py, test_distance.py (with the tests/data/*.txt matrices, BSD), test_hausdorff.py, test_spherical_voronoi.py, test_slerp.py, test__procrustes.py, transform/tests/*. degenerate_pointset.npz and selfdual-4d-polytope.txt are part of the corpus. Equality as section 4 states it, per component; differences are listed by name, never summarised as a count. Invariants checked with exact predicates on every output: Euler characteristic, every Delaunay simplex positively oriented and with an empty circumsphere (except where Qhull reports coplanar), hull convexity, neighbour symmetry, Voronoi duality, k-NN results equal to brute force (as multisets of distances). Degenerate corpora: duplicates, collinear / coplanar / cospherical sets, integer lattices, nearly-degenerate tilted lattices (Shewchuk’s “tilted grid”), points at ±1e±300, mixed scales, QJ restarts.
data.7-performance-plan#7. Performance plan:
Single core against SciPy 1.18.1 (workers=1, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1), interleaved rounds, never at 1-min load above 8, allocation counts reported.
Table Sizes Delaunay 2-D, 3-D; ConvexHull 3-D, 6-D; Voronoi 2-D n = 10³, 10⁴, 10⁵, 10⁶ (10⁵ in 6-D) KDTree build, query k = 1, 16, query_ball_point, count_neighbors n = 10⁶, d = 3; n = 10⁵, d = 16 cdist/pdist per metric 1000 × 1000, d = 3, 64, 1024 Rotation apply, as_euler, from_matrix, * 10⁶ rotations Order: port exactly, measure, then optimise where the table shows a gap, algorithm first. Qhull’s mem_r.c free lists become per-run slabs, qset_r sets become slices with the same element order. distance SIMD kernels go into go-simd (the lowest shared library), vectorised across pairs. Slower than SciPy is an open defect.
data.8-security-and-fuzzing#8. Security and f: Untrusted input: NaN refused (as SciPy); ±Inf refused too, a deliberate divergence (SciPy checks only NaN, _qhull.pyx:284, and hands infinities to Qhull). Option strings: the Qhull option parser is fuzzed; file and trace options (TO, TI, TR, Tn output to a file) are refused. Resource bounds: Delaunay output grows as n^⌈d/2⌉; every Qhull run takes a facet budget and a context.Context and returns a refusal, never an out-of-memory. Dimension limit 64 (NPY_MAXDIMS in _qhull.pyx), checked before allocation. KDTree recursion depth is bounded (the non-compact degenerate path re-enters build), leafsize ≥ 1, k ≤ n. 32-bit overflow: Qhull ids are int; SciPy stores indices as intc. Counts above 2³¹−1 are refused; pdist length n(n−1)/2 is computed with checked multiplication; squareform validates sizes before allocating. Bomb tests assert a refusal under GOMEMLIMIT and ulimit -v. Fuzz targets: option parser, every constructor (points as raw bytes → float64), find_simplex, KDTree build+query, from_euler sequences, squareform, predicates (sign against math/big exact evaluation).
data.9-waves-and-tasks-one-pull-request-each#:
W0, foundations
T0.1 go-ndarray linalg: export getrf/getrs, add gecon + lacn2 (LAPACK dgecon parity). T0.2 Oracle harness (Go): pinned SciPy 1.18.1 wheels, fixture writer, JSON schema. Q0/K0 Measurement: FMA contraction in SciPy’s arm64 build; libc++ vs libstdc++ in each wheel; tree.indices equality on 100 random sets. W1, predicates 4. P1 Expansion arithmetic, Orient2D, InCircle (adaptive stages A–D). 5. P2 Orient3D, InSphere. 6. P3 Exact n-D orientation and in-sphere. 7. P4 Fuzz against math/big, benchmark against predicates.c, cross-arch bit test.
W2, distance 8. D1 Minkowski family kernels (euclidean, sqeuclidean, cityblock, chebyshev, minkowski, weighted). 9. D2 braycurtis, canberra and the boolean metrics. 10. D3 correlation, cosine, seuclidean, mahalanobis, jensenshannon (C kernels). 11. D4 pdist, cdist, callables, out=, squareform, is_valid_*, num_obs_*. 12. D5 Single-pair functions and directed_hausdorff. 13. D6 go-simd kernels across pairs; performance table.
W3, kdtree 14. K1 Build: sliding midpoint, median, compact, periodic boxsize, libc++ partition/nth_element, node view. 15. K2 query (k list, eps, p, upper bound, workers). 16. K3 query_ball_point, query_ball_tree, query_pairs. 17. K4 count_neighbors, sparse_distance_matrix (all output types). 18. K5 Rectangle, minkowski_distance(_p), distance_matrix; fuzz; performance table.
W4, qhull 19. Q1 Sets, memory, random, option parser (refusals). 20. Q2 Geometry (geom_r, geom2_r). 21. Q3 Polyhedra and the Quickhull core (poly_r, poly2_r, libqhull_r), Qt. 22. Q4 Merging (merge_r): Qx, Q12, Qc, coplanar points. 23. Q5 Delaunay mode: d, Qbb, Qz, Qu. 24. Q6 Voronoi mode (v, the io_r subset). 25. Q7 Halfspace mode (H, SciPy’s feaspoint patch). 26. Q8 Joggle QJ and restarts. 27. Q9 Incremental mode (add_points, restart, Q11); fuzz; bomb tests.
W5, spatial 28. S1 ConvexHull. 29. S2 Delaunay and Tsearch. 30. S3 Voronoi. 31. S4 HalfspaceIntersection. 32. S5 SphericalVoronoi. 33. S6 Procrustes, GeometricSlerp; performance table; v0.1.0 of the facade.
W6, transform 34. R1 Rotation core (quat, matrix per Markley 2008, rotvec, mrp, apply, compose, inverse, magnitude, canonical). 35. R2 Euler and Davenport angles. 36. R3 mean, reduce, approx_equal, align_vectors, random, create_group, concatenate, power. 37. R4 N-D array-API backend. 38. R5 RigidTransform. 39. R6 Slerp, RotationSpline (after solve_banded).
W7, triangulation (MATLAB delta) 40. M1 Triangulation and its queries. 41. M2 DelaunayTriangulation 2-D/3-D (incremental insertion on exact predicates), isInterior, convexHull, voronoiDiagram. 42. M3 2-D constrained edges (shared with item 13). 43. M4 AlphaShape 2-D/3-D (after opening the full Edelsbrunner–Mücke paper). 44. M5 convhull/convhulln (Simplify), delaunay/delaunayn, voronoin via qhull; inpolygon, polyarea. 45. M6 KDTreeSearcher, ExhaustiveSearcher, createns, knnsearch (IncludeTies), rangesearch, pdist2 (Smallest/Largest).
Waves W1, W2, W3 and W6 are independent and may run in parallel; W4 needs nothing but itself; W5 needs W4 and W3; W7 needs W1 and W3. Consumers: go-approx scattered interpolation and RBF (W5 S2, W3), optimize shgo (W5 S2, S1), stats QMC Lloyd (W5 S3, W3), item 13 meshing (W1, W7 M3).

data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be: Combinatorial validity: the Euler relation, and the empty-circumsphere test with exact predicates. The vertex set equals the oracle’s up to degeneracies; the number of differing simplices is reported only for cocircular input, where non-uniqueness is legitimate.

Status: planned (wave 2). There is no repository and no code yet, and nearest is a working name. These pages describe the plan, not a release. The design proposes to replace this working name with go-geometry/kdtree, an exact port of SciPy’s cKDTree rather than an adoption of gonum’s tree, so that results and tie order match SciPy.
k-d trees and exact nearest-neighbour search.

Status: released, v0.1.0. Repository go-geometry/predicates, wave W1 of the design (tasks P1 to P4).
go get github.com/go-geometry/predicates@v0.1.0 import "github.com/go-geometry/predicates" predicates.Orient2D(a, b, c) // > 0 counterclockwise, < 0 clockwise, 0 collinear predicates.InCircle(a, b, c, d) // > 0 if d is inside the circle through a, b, c (ccw) predicates.Orient3D(a, b, c, d) // > 0 if d is below the plane of a, b, c predicates.InSphere(a, b, c, d, e) // > 0 if e is inside the sphere through a..d (Orient3D > 0) predicates.OrientN(points) // d+1 points in d dimensions, 1 <= d <= 16 predicates.InSphereN(points) // d+2 points in d dimensions
data.depends-on#Depends on: Nothing outside the Go standard library.
data.how-it-is-validated#How it is validated: The sign of every predicate equals the sign of the determinant computed with big.Rat on random, near-degenerate (rounded onto a line, circle, plane or sphere, then nudged by a few ulps), exactly degenerate (collinear and coplanar lattices, Pythagorean circles and spheres, repeated points under inexact translations), Shewchuk’s tilted grid, and huge / tiny / mixed-magnitude input: zero mismatches. The non-robust Fast evaluation is wrong on hundreds of these cases, so the corpus is hard. Planted breaks: with the stage A or stage B error bound removed, the same corpus must produce wrong signs, or the test fails. Fuzz targets for every predicate check the sign against big.Rat; their corpus is committed. 100 % statement coverage, -race, govulncheck. Against Shewchuk’s predicates.c (cgo, bench/): equal signs on every benchmark input.
data.reference-implementation-and-licence#Ref: Implementation Licence and use Shewchuk’s predicates.c public domain; the package is written from it and the paper (https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~quake/robust.html) The package is BSD-3-Clause.
data.references#References: Reference Cite Shewchuk, Adaptive Precision Floating-Point Arithmetic and Fast Robust Geometric Predicates, Discrete Comput. Geom. 18:305-363, 1997 doi:10.1007/PL00009321
data.what-it-provides#What it provides: Function Method Orient2D, InCircle, Orient3D, InSphere adaptive precision (Shewchuk 1997): a floating-point filter with a proven error bound (stage A), then the exact determinant of the rounded differences (B), a first-order tail correction (C) and the exact determinant (D), each only when the previous stage cannot certify the sign ...Exact the exact determinant directly ...Fast plain floating-point evaluation, not robust, for comparison OrientN, InSphereN exact sign in any dimension 1 ≤ d ≤ 16: floating-point expansion determinants up to order 8, fraction-free big-integer elimination above Exact sign for every finite input. Each predicate checks that its coordinates lie in a range, set by the degree of its determinant, in which floating-point expansions cannot overflow or underflow; outside it, an exact big-integer evaluation answers. NaN or ±Inf gives NaN (OrientN/InSphereN return ErrNotFinite). Identical bits on every architecture: every product is rounded by an explicit float64(...) conversion, so the Go compiler never fuses it into an FMA. A test hashes the bits of 5 600 results and compares the hash on amd64, arm64, riscv64, loong64, ppc64le, s390x, 386 and arm. Bounded cost: MaxDim = 16. With coordinates spread over the whole float64 exponent range, the exact elimination took 40 ms at d = 16, 0.9 s at d = 32 and 56 s at d = 64.
